summary: Configured node1 as the cluster’s internal NTP source and node2 to synchronize exclusively from node1. Both nodes retained Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210, survived serial restarts, and are currently synchronized and healthy.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu Xenial-compatible ntpd on both nodes.
Configured node1 to serve NTP on 10.100.229.10:123 with restricted internal-subnet access.
Configured node2 with only `server 10.100.229.10 iburst prefer`.
Disabled systemd-timesyncd to prevent parallel public synchronization.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities, persisted configuration, and recovered synchronization.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the legacy operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 were observed initially; the same kernel remains after both restarts.

evidence.requirement: Configure node1 as the internal time source
evidence.summary: node1 has enabled, active ntpd listening on 10.100.229.10:123, permits the internal /24, and is synchronized at stratum 2.

evidence.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize from node1 instead of a public server
evidence.summary: node2’s sole configured source is 10.100.229.10; it selects node1, reports leap=00 and stratum 3, and has healthy kernel NTP status.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID 0d49f077…, restart acknowledgment, changed boot ID bc1b79a4…, recovered service/listener/configuration, and node2 reselecting node1 before proceeding.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID 6ab98831…, restart acknowledgment, changed boot ID 9556cfd2…, unchanged configuration checksum, and recovered synchronization from node1.

evidence.requirement: Final cluster health after all restarts
evidence.summary: Both ntpd services are active and enabled, timesyncd is inactive, node1 is stratum 2, and node2 selects node1 at stratum 3.
